title: Meet the coaches, measurers, and builders carving out a slice of the AI cost-saving business
excerpt: Companies are struggling to rein in AI spending. Here are the people helping them slash their bills.
content_html:
Don't use Swiss Army knives for surgically precise work; use scalpels.

That's what Manos Koukoumidis and other players in the AI cost-saving business say is the biggest problem with how companies use AI. They're using the most powerful, versatile, and expensive AI models — from frontier labs like Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google — to handle niche tasks within their organizations.

Koukoumidis, the CEO of the Washington-based AI company Oumi AI, called this practice "widely irrational and inefficient," resulting in staggering AI bills.

Founded in 2024, Oumi lets individuals vibe-code their own niche AI models within minutes, tailored to their tasks and goals. It raised $10 million in its 2024 seed round.

Oumi is one of the many companies that have sprung up in the last two years to solve the biggest enterprise problem of the day: reducing highly inflated enterprise AI spending and increasing its returns on investment. As companies move away from the tokenmaxxing trend — where employees were encouraged to burn as many AI tokens as they could — these cost-saving services are becoming increasingly sought after.

Some of these companies are consulting firms and measurement platforms that advise clients on integrating AI into their workflows in a smart way. Others, like Oumi, are building new products, such as model builders and inference platforms, to tackle the problem from the source.

The coaches

The first category is the coaches: the consultants and advisors lighting up the path to AI success.

Sydney-based business consultancy Adaptovate has been operating for more than eight years, with over 100 consultants across offices around the world. But over the past three years, the company has zeroed in on helping others get the most bang for their AI spending buck.

Michael Murphy, a partner in the company, said Adaptovate works with clients at all stages of their AI adoption journey — from a snacks manufacturer that's just figuring out how to use AI in its supply chain, to a 30,000-employee-strong professional services company that wants to restructure all its teams around GenAI products.

"It always starts with the strategy," Murphy said. "Figuring out how decision-making changes. How does your talent model change? How does your organization's structure change when you're beginning to scale AI across the full organization?

The measurers

Then there are the measurers, who use software tools to help companies pinpoint where AI is working for them and where it isn't.

One example is the San Francisco-based Larridin. CTO Ameya Kanitkar told Business Insider that the company acts as a measurement layer across its clients' AI tools, employees, agents, and spending.

One of Larridin's products is a data analysis tool that shows how employee productivity varies with token spend, helping companies identify the sweet spot for the token budget they allocate to their staff.

Kanitkar, who has worked at LinkedIn, Coinbase, and Groupon, said Larridin got off to a slow start because companies weren't particularly concerned about AI spending in the early days of adoption. But that has shifted after they started pouring millions into the resource, and he's seeing Larridin's traction double every quarter since the start of the year.

"It just makes sense that you need a measurement layer to make sure that all those hundreds of millions of dollars you're spending are actually justified and are properly spent," he said.

Larridin raised $17 million in seed funding from Andreessen Horowitz, Bloomberg Beta, Google Ventures, and other investors and launched the platform in 2025. It now serves clients from data center construction companies to biosciences and financial services firms.

The builders

The third category is the builders: the startups like Oumi that are creating products to directly help companies slash AI costs.

Another example is Runware, a company cofounded by serial entrepreneur Ioana Hreninciuc. Runware provides the inference infrastructure companies need to run AI models quickly, cost-effectively, and at scale. This makes it much easier for companies to scale up their AI products without worrying about AI outages.

For those buying their own GPUs, there's Tensormesh. The startup focuses on Key-Value Cache, cofounder Junchen Jiang said, something that "never appears in people's token bills" but certainly affects their costs.

Tensormesh's caching system helps businesses "accept more queries on fewer GPUs," Jiang said. The company raised $20 million from big-hitters in hardware like AMD and NVentures, Nvidia's venture capital arm.

And even more are gestating, ready to hit the market. Conifer is still participating in Y Combinator's summer 2026 batch. Its cofounder, Charles Muehlberger, said the company had already raised $1.3 million, about 20% of its desired raise, before Demo Day. The company's product will synthesize queries, break them into pieces, and feed the pieces to different models (including local ones).

"We think the main customer is one who is focused on cost," said Michael Jeffords, Conifer's other cofounder.

Bottom line

While the coaches, measurers, and builders are cutting the AI-cost-saving pie in different ways, their advice is largely the same: stop using frontier AI models for every menial task, start using lighter, open-source models, and build your own models to reduce costs and reliance on the big AI labs.

They're also proposing new ways to think of ROI. Kanitkar from Larridin said AI costs should be treated as capital expenditures, not operating expenses, and companies shouldn't expect to see gains immediately, but rather over a period of a year or two.

They're all united on one belief — that companies jumped on the AI hype train without proper planning, and most don't really know what they're doing.

"Everybody's pretending their AI spending is paying off," Hreninciuc from Runware said.

"The incentive right now is for people to say it is paying off and to find a way to justify it, and because of this, we don't have an accurate view of the market, as nobody wants to be the canary in the coal mine," she said.

sentences.en: While the coaches, measurers, and builders are cutting the AI-cost-saving pie in different ways, their advice is largely the same: stop using frontier AI models for every menial task, start using lighter, open-source models, and build your own models to reduce costs and reliance on the big AI labs.
sentences.zh: 虽然教练、测量者和构建者以不同的方式切分人工智能成本节约蛋糕，但他们的建议基本上是相同的：停止在每项琐碎任务中使用前沿人工智能模型，开始使用更轻的开源模型，并构建自己的模型以降低成本和对大型人工智能实验室的依赖。

blocks.html_en: They're also proposing new ways to think of ROI. Kanitkar from Larridin said AI costs should be treated as capital expenditures, not operating expenses, and companies shouldn't expect to see gains immediately, but rather over a period of a year or two.

sentences.en: They're also proposing new ways to think of ROI.
sentences.zh: 他们还提出了考虑投资回报率的新方法。

sentences.en: Kanitkar from Larridin said AI costs should be treated as capital expenditures, not operating expenses, and companies shouldn't expect to see gains immediately, but rather over a period of a year or two.
sentences.zh: Larridin 的 Kanitkar 表示，人工智能成本应被视为资本支出，而不是运营支出，公司不应指望立即看到收益，而应该在一两年内看到收益。

blocks.html_en: They're all united on one belief — that companies jumped on the AI hype train without proper planning, and most don't really know what they're doing.

sentences.en: They're all united on one belief — that companies jumped on the AI hype train without proper planning, and most don't really know what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 他们都坚信一个信念：公司在没有适当规划的情况下就跳上了人工智能炒作的列车，而且大多数公司并不真正知道自己在做什么。

blocks.html_en: "Everybody's pretending their AI spending is paying off," Hreninciuc from Runware said.

sentences.en: "Everybody's pretending their AI spending is paying off," Hreninciuc from Runware said.
sentences.zh: Runware 的 Hreninciuc 表示：“每个人都假装他们的人工智能支出正在得到回报。”

blocks.html_en: "The incentive right now is for people to say it is paying off and to find a way to justify it, and because of this, we don't have an accurate view of the market, as nobody wants to be the canary in the coal mine," she said.

content_html_zh:
不要使用瑞士军刀进行外科手术般的精确工作；使用手术刀。

马诺斯·库库米迪斯 (Manos Koukoumidis) 和人工智能成本节约行业的其他参与者表示，这是企业如何使用人工智能的最大问题。 他们使用来自 Anthropic、OpenAI 和 Google 等前沿实验室的最强大、最通用和最昂贵的人工智能模型来处理组织内的利基任务。

总部位于华盛顿的人工智能公司 Oumi AI 的首席执行官 Koukoumidis 称这种做法“非常不合理且效率低下”，导致人工智能费用惊人。

Oumi 成立于 2024 年，可让个人在几分钟内根据自己的任务和目标定制自己的小众人工智能模型。 它在 2024 年种子轮融资中筹集了 1000 万美元。

Oumi 是过去两年中涌现的众多公司之一，它们致力于解决当今最大的企业问题：减少高度膨胀的企业人工智能支出并提高投资回报率。 随着公司摆脱代币最大化趋势（鼓励员工尽可能多地销毁人工智能代币），这些节省成本的服务正变得越来越受欢迎。

其中一些公司是咨询公司和测量平台，建议客户以智能方式将人工智能集成到他们的工作流程中。 Oumi 等其他公司正在开发新产品，例如模型构建器和推理平台，以从源头上解决问题。

教练们

第一类是教练：照亮人工智能成功之路的顾问和顾问。

总部位于悉尼的商业咨询公司 Adaptovate 已运营八年多，在世界各地设有办事处，拥有 100 多名顾问。 但在过去的三年里，该公司专注于帮助其他人从人工智能支出中获得最大收益。

该公司合伙人 Michael Murphy 表示，Adaptovate 在客户采用人工智能的各个阶段都与客户合作，从一家刚刚弄清楚如何在其供应链中使用人工智能的零食制造商，到一家拥有 30,000 名员工、希望围绕 GenAI 产品重组所有团队的专业服务公司。

“一切总是从战略开始，”墨菲说。 “弄清楚决策如何变化。 您的人才模式发生了怎样的变化？ 当您开始在整个组织中扩展人工智能时，您的组织结构会发生怎样的变化？

测量者

然后是测量人员，他们使用软件工具帮助公司确定人工智能在哪些方面对他们有用，哪些方面不适用。

旧金山的 Larridin 就是一个例子。 首席技术官 Ameya Kanitkar 告诉《商业内幕》，该公司充当客户人工智能工具、员工、代理和支出的衡量层。

Larridin 的产品之一是一种数据分析工具，它显示员工生产力如何随代币支出变化，帮助公司确定分配给员工的代币预算的最佳点。

曾在 LinkedIn、Coinbase 和 Groupon 工作过的 Kanitkar 表示，Larridin 起步缓慢，因为公司在采用人工智能的早期并不特别担心人工智能的支出。 但在他们开始向该资源投入数百万美元后，这种情况发生了变化，他看到自今年年初以来，Larridin 的吸引力每个季度都翻倍。

他说：“你需要一个衡量层来确保你花费的数亿美元实际上是合理的并且得到了正确的使用，这是有道理的。”

Larridin 从 Andreessen Horowitz、Bloomberg Beta、Google Ventures 和其他投资者那里筹集了 1700 万美元的种子资金，并于 2025 年推出了该平台。 它现在为从数据中心建设公司到生物科学和金融服务公司的客户提供服务。

建设者们

第三类是建设者：像Oumi这样的初创公司正在创造产品来直接帮助公司削减人工智能成本。

另一个例子是 Runware，这是一家由连续创业者 Ioana Hreninciuc 联合创立的公司。 Runware 为公司提供了快速、经济高效、大规模运行 AI 模型所需的推理基础设施。 这使得公司可以更轻松地扩展其人工智能产品，而不必担心人工智能中断。

对于那些购买自己的 GPU 的人来说，可以选择 Tensormesh。 联合创始人Junchen Jiang表示，这家初创公司专注于键值缓存，这“永远不会出现在人们的代币账单中”，但肯定会影响他们的成本。

Jiang 表示，Tensormesh 的缓存系统可以帮助企业“在更少的 GPU 上接受更多的查询”。 该公司从 AMD 和 Nvidia 风险投资部门 NVentures 等硬件领域的巨头那里筹集了 2000 万美元。

还有更多的产品正在酝酿之中，准备投放市场。 Conifer 仍在参与 Y Combinator 的 2026 年夏季批次。 其联合创始人 Charles Muehlberger 表示，在演示日之前，该公司已经筹集了 130 万美元，约占预期融资额的 20%。 该公司的产品将综合查询，将其分解为多个片段，并将这些片段提供给不同的模型（包括本地模型）。

“我们认为主要客户是注重成本的客户，”Conifer 的另一位联合创始人迈克尔·杰福兹 (Michael Jeffords) 说。

底线

虽然教练、测量者和构建者以不同的方式切分人工智能成本节约蛋糕，但他们的建议基本上是相同的：停止在每项琐碎任务中使用前沿人工智能模型，开始使用更轻的开源模型，并构建自己的模型以降低成本和对大型人工智能实验室的依赖。

他们还提出了考虑投资回报率的新方法。 Larridin 的 Kanitkar 表示，人工智能成本应被视为资本支出，而不是运营支出，公司不应指望立即看到收益，而应该在一两年内看到收益。

他们都坚信一个信念：公司在没有适当规划的情况下就跳上了人工智能炒作的列车，而且大多数公司并不真正知道自己在做什么。

Runware 的 Hreninciuc 表示：“每个人都假装他们的人工智能支出正在得到回报。”

“现在的动机是让人们说它正在得到回报，并找到一种方法来证明它的合理性，正因为如此，我们对市场没有准确的看法，因为没有人想成为煤矿里的金丝雀，”她说。
